name: ava-research-docs
description: Studies under research/: one researcher's methodology and evidence, written for a global reader who meets the project for the first time. Casual lead-ins, technical lists; the two never mix.

rules.name: plain-headings
rules.description: A one-word heading carries no article.
criteria: No heading reads 'The X' where X is one word. Write 'X'.

rules.name: no-assumed-context
rules.description: Every entity or state the study references is one a global reader meeting the project for the first time can place.
criteria: For each term, tool, group, prior event, or state the study references, ask: does a global first-time reader know what this refers to? If no, a Background section at the start of the document establishes it before first use.
Context too long or too far off topic for the Background section goes to an appendix, with a citation.

rules.name: shared-understanding-up-front
rules.description: The introduction and Background sections introduce the terminology the rest of the study uses, and the jargon load stays level across sections.
criteria: Every term that more than one section uses appears in the introduction or the Background section first.
The jargon density of one section does not depart wildly from the density of the whole document or of the other studies.

anchors.1: Terms appear without introduction and each section speaks its own dialect.
anchors.3: Most shared terms are introduced up front; one section runs much denser than the rest.
anchors.5: Every shared term is introduced up front and every section reads at the same density.

rules.name: first-person-researcher
rules.description: The study speaks as one individual doing the research: first person for the author's own experience, explicit third person for outside persons and communities.
criteria: The author's own actions, corpora, observations, and decisions use first person.
Outside work names its source in explicit third person: existing research, the corpus-linguistics community, a cited author.
No sentence refers to the author's own experience as 'the author', 'one author', or 'the study' where 'I' is the actor.

rules.name: global-audience
rules.description: The study names no other person, private corpus, or customer content.
criteria: No sentence names another person, a handle, or a private corpus by its source name.
Every corpus appears by type and size.
No sentence quotes customer content.

rules.name: five-parts
rules.description: Each study states the question, the method, the data by type and size, the result, and the decisions it produced. The directory index is exempt.
criteria: A heading marks each of the five parts in every study document.
The data section gives a document count and a token or word count for each corpus.
The decisions section names the shipped behavior each decision produced.
The directory index lists the studies and carries no parts of its own.

rules.name: evidence-first
rules.description: Every claim of a difference and every parameter choice rests on a measured value or a named run.
criteria: A claim that two groups differ cites the measured rates.
A parameter value comes with the reason for that value.
A claim the study did not measure says so.

anchors.3: Most claims cite a number; some rest on impression.
anchors.5: Every claim traces to a measurement, a count, or a named script.

rules.name: shipped-paths-only
rules.description: Every path, command, flag, and rule id the study names exists in the repository.
criteria: No sentence points at a local-only directory or an unshipped file.
Every rule id the study names as shipped appears in the check catalog.
A rule the study names as dropped is marked as dropped in the same sentence.
